request: The fixture starter's page shows only a bare heading, so there is no way to tell which starter was opened or which version it is. Add a small one-line version badge under the page heading on the '/' route that reads "fixture 0.1.0" (the starter id and version from starter.json), and make sure the starter still builds and the page still loads.

plan.goal: Show which starter and version the fixture starter is, so a reader can tell at a glance from the page itself.

scope.title: Version badge on the '/' page
scope.description: Add a one-line visible badge under the page heading that reads "fixture 0.1.0", matching the embedded starter descriptor (pkg/starters/data/fixture/starter.json).

steps.description: Add an element with data-testid="starter-badge" directly under the page heading in index.html.
Have src/main.js set the badge text to the starter id and version, "fixture 0.1.0".

out_of_scope.item: More routes or pages on the fixture starter
out_of_scope.reason: The fixture starter is a single-page, test-only starter; extra routes belong to a larger task size (SP-154 §154a: small change, new feature, from-scratch app).

out_of_scope.item: Reading the starter id and version from starter.json at runtime
out_of_scope.reason: The fixture's badge may hard-code the value; runtime manifest reading is product-starter work (SP-153 §153c), not part of this small change.
